title: Decree 15 sets the Lebanese nationality regime
why: Mandate-era nationality decree; its paternal-line rule still shapes citizenship and mixed-family rights.

title: Code of Obligations and Contracts enacted
why: Civil-law backbone of contract and tort, French-inspired and still in force with amendments.

title: Arrete 60 LR recognises religious communities and their courts
why: Mandate order that entrenched sect-based personal status jurisdiction later kept by the Republic.

title: Penal Code promulgated by decree-law
why: Criminal code in force for decades; provisions such as Article 534 and former Article 522 drew later reform fights.

title: Druze community law on personal status
why: Sect-specific family law for the Druze, later amended in 2017 by the community's own authorities. (corrected from 1948)

title: Charles Malik helps draft the Universal Declaration of Human Rights
why: Lebanese diplomat shaped the text; Lebanon's early role in UN rights law.

title: Forest Law regulates use and protection of forests
why: Mandate-to-republic forest code; a base for later fire and logging rules.

title: Law of 2 April 1951 delimiting competences of Christian and Jewish confessional authorities
why: Defines which matters go to religious courts versus civil courts; the legal frame of the confessional court system. (corrected from 'Law on the jurisdiction of religious sects'; law covers Christian and Jewish communities)

title: Jaafari Shia personal status courts regulated by law
why: Gave the Shia community its own organised courts and personal status rules.

title: Normandy dump on Beirut's shore begins receiving municipal waste and rubble
why: Sea-filled dump of war debris and waste, later capped and built over by Solidere. (corrected from 1978; paper says random disposal began around 1975, large demolition debris 1982-83)

title: Constitutional Law 18 adds Constitutional Council to the Constitution
why: The 1990 revision of Article 19 provided for a Constitutional Council to review statutes.

title: Treaty of Brotherhood, Cooperation and Coordination with Syria signed
why: Post-Taif bilateral treaty, cited by both sides in later debates on Syrian influence and its 2005 aftermath.

title: 1992 election held for 128 seats with Christian-Muslim parity
why: Parity between Christians and Muslims/Druze fixed at 64-64; many Christians boycotted, a long-running legitimacy grievance.

title: Horsh Ehden reserve established by law
why: One of Lebanon's first statutory nature reserves, home to cedar and rare fir stands.

title: Law 216 creates the Ministry of Environment
why: First ministry dedicated to the environment; its powers were later set out in Law 444/2002.

title: Law 250 sets up the Constitutional Council
why: Gave Lebanon a body to review statutes and election disputes, first seated in 1994.

title: Constitutional Council begins work
why: First court able to annul laws; its later rulings on term extensions and taxes became key precedents.

title: Lebanon accedes to UN climate and biodiversity conventions
why: Joined UNFCCC and the CBD in the post-war treaty push.

title: Sukleen takes over Beirut-Mount Lebanon waste collection
why: Private contract that fed the Naameh landfill and the 2015 crisis when it lapsed.

title: Decision 52/1 sets national air-quality and emission standards
why: First legal limits on air pollutants; weakly enforced since. (sources conflict: MoE strategy dates Decision 52/1 12/09/1996; some documents give July 1996)

title: Tyre Coast Nature Reserve created by law
why: Protects a nesting beach for sea turtles; a Ramsar site listing followed.

title: Hrawi tables optional civil marriage bill; cabinet approves
why: Approved by cabinet, then blocked by religious authorities, it became the template for every later civil-status bill. (corrected from 1998-03; month unconfirmed)

title: Law 140 protects secrecy of communications
why: First statute on interception and privacy of communications, later cited in surveillance debates.

title: Aammiq wetland and Tyre coast join Ramsar list
why: Lebanon's first wetlands of international importance.

title: Electoral law 171/2000 governs the 2000 and 2005 elections
why: Used for the 2000 election; the Syrian-era districting was widely criticised and revisited in 2005. (corrected from 'sets small districts for 2000 vote'; source says mid-sized districts)

title: Telecom Law 431 creates framework for liberalisation and a regulator
why: Set up the Telecommunications Regulatory Authority idea; its full implementation stalled for years.

title: UN Security Council Resolution 1559 calls for foreign forces to leave
why: Underpinned the Syrian withdrawal and disarmament debate that shaped later legal fights.

title: UN Security Council creates the Hariri investigation commission
why: UNIIIC began the international probe that led to the Special Tribunal for Lebanon.

title: Lebanon accedes to the Kyoto Protocol
why: Non-Annex I party with no binding targets; enabled carbon-credit projects.

title: UN Security Council Resolution 1701 ends the July war
why: Legal basis for UNIFIL's enlarged mandate and the south Litani arrangements.

title: UNEP publishes Lebanon post-conflict environmental assessment
why: Covered the Jiyeh oil spill and war debris; the model for later assessments.

title: STL agreement enters into force
why: The tribunal's treaty basis took effect after Resolution 1757 was invoked on 30 May.

title: Electoral law 25/2008 adopted after Doha
why: Returned to the kaza as district with 1960-style boundaries for 2009; Beirut split in three.

title: Jabal Moussa designated a UNESCO biosphere reserve
why: Community-managed reserve in Keserwan; a counterweight to quarrying pressure.

title: Lebanon accedes to the UN Convention against Corruption
why: Basis for later asset-recovery and disclosure laws (2020-21).

title: STL pre-trial judge orders release of four generals
why: Ended four years of detention without charge and weakened the early case.

title: Parliamentary election held under 2008 law
why: Held 7 June 2009 under the Doha-era kaza system.

title: National Water Sector Strategy adopted
why: Planned dams and lakes to cut the summer deficit; Bisri later grew out of it. (corrected from 2010-03; strategy prepared 2010, government endorsed it 2012 by Resolution 2 of 9 Mar 2012)

title: STL prosecutor files first indictment confidentially
why: Opened the case against four suspects, confirmed in June 2011.

title: STL confirms indictment of four suspects
why: Named Ayyash, Badreddine, Oneissi and Sabra; Lebanon said it could not arrest them.

title: Decree 8633 makes environmental impact assessments mandatory
why: Required EIAs for major projects; quarry and resort disputes later hinged on it.

title: Constitutional Council fails to rule on parliament's first term extension
why: Quorum was not reached, so the 17-month extension stood, a precedent for later extensions.

title: First civil marriage registered in Lebanon after a contested ministry ruling
why: Couple Darwish and Sukkarieh wed without sect; registration fights showed the gap in civil-status law.

title: STL indicts Hassan Merhi in a connected case
why: Added a fifth accused; joined with the Oneissi case later.

title: Civil campaign mobilises to keep Dalieh of Raouche public
why: Coalition contested private fencing of the shore headland.

title: STL trial opens in absentia in The Hague
why: Prosecution opened against Ayyash, Badreddine, Oneissi and Sabra, none in custody.

title: Badreddine reported killed in Damascus; STL later ends his case
why: Removed the highest-profile accused and narrowed the eventual trial.

title: Law 63 sets up Litani Basin depollution plan
why: Gave the Litani River Authority power to prosecute polluters and earmarked about USD 730 million for cleanup.

title: Parliament amends the Druze personal status law (Law 58)
why: Reform by the highest Druze religious authorities, not parliament, illustrating sect-by-sect change. (corrected from 'Reform by the highest Druze religious authorities, not parliament': search results say Parliament passed Law 58 on 19 Sept 2017 amending 16 articles of the 1948 code)

title: Council of State orders a freeze on the Eden Bay resort
why: After Green Line's suit, the court halted building at Ramlet al-Baida until legality was checked.

title: Constitutional Council annuls the 2017 tax law financing the pay scale
why: Struck down tax provisions for procedural defects, forcing a re-vote; an early test of the Council's budget role. (corrected from April 2017: annulled 22 Sept 2017 because not passed within the annual budget process)

title: Council of State reverses its freeze; Eden Bay building resumes
why: It gave no reasons; campaigners called it a blow to public access to the shore.

title: Parliament repeals Penal Code Article 522
why: Ended the rule letting a rapist escape punishment by marrying the victim; a Legal Agenda-era campaign win. (law number unconfirmed)

title: Parliament passes Air Quality Protection Law
why: Set a framework for emission monitoring; implementing decrees lagged.

title: Integrated Solid Waste Management Law enacted
why: Favoured decentralised, sorted waste handling; open dumps and burning persisted.

title: Water Law updates the legal framework for water resources
why: Aimed to consolidate water governance; implementation stayed thin.

title: Total, Eni, Novatek sign offshore Block 4 and 9 agreements
why: First licensing round awards; drilling in Block 4 in 2020 and Block 9 in 2023 found no commercial gas.

title: Law 81/2018 on e-transactions and personal data promulgated
why: Lebanon's only data-protection and cybercrime text; effective 31 Mar 2019, no independent data authority.

title: Law 81/2018 takes effect
why: Cybercrime offences (illegal access, data interference) and data rules became enforceable, overseen by the Economy Ministry.

title: Tripoli by-election after a Constitutional Council annulment
why: The Council's review of a disputed Sunni seat forced a re-run, showing its election-court role.

title: Judge Fadi Sawan appointed to lead port blast inquiry
why: First lead investigator; he later charged a caretaker PM and ex-ministers before removal.

title: Sawan charges PM Diab and three ex-ministers with negligence
why: First charges against senior politicians; ministers denied wrongdoing and challenged his jurisdiction.

title: STL sentences Salim Ayyash to life
why: Sentenced after the 18 Aug conviction; he remains at large, the first STL conviction.

title: Wildfire season averages about 170 fires and 1,500 ha a year
why: Reported range for 2021-2023 before wartime burns raised totals.

title: Judge Tarek Bitar takes over the port blast investigation
why: He charged officials, sought immunity waivers and faced repeated legal challenges.

title: Court of Cassation removes Judge Sawan from the port blast case
why: After ministers' complaints of bias; the file moved to a new investigator.

title: Swiss prosecutors open a probe linked to Salameh and BDL
why: First foreign criminal proceeding tied to central-bank transfers; later joined by France, Germany and Luxembourg. (corrected from 2021-03: Swiss AG announced the probe in January 2021)

title: Tleil fuel-tank explosion in Akkar
why: Army seized hoarded fuel; blast amid shortages killed dozens and became a symbol of the crisis.

title: Tayouneh clashes during protest against Judge Bitar
why: Gunfire at a Hezbollah-Amal protest killed seven people and deepened the fight over the inquiry.

title: Bitar's port blast investigation effectively frozen
why: Legal challenges by ex-ministers and a cabinet standoff halted sessions for about 13 months.

title: STL appeal verdicts: Merhi and Oneissi get life in absentia
why: Final STL convictions in the Hariri case; all convicts remain at large.

title: France, Germany and Luxembourg freeze about EUR 120 million in Salameh-linked assets
why: European joint action, after a Eurojust-backed probe, to preserve suspected embezzlement proceeds.

title: Parliamentary election under the 2017 proportional law
why: Second vote with 15 districts; produced a fragmented parliament with no clear majority.

title: Cholera returns to Lebanon after about 30 years
why: Outbreak tied to failing water and sanitation; centred on Akkar and Bekaa.

title: Bitar resumes port blast probe after 13 months
why: He charged more officials; the prosecutor countercharged him and freed detainees, reigniting the dispute.

title: Israeli fire and munitions burn about 16,000 ha in south
why: Reported figure since hostilities began; white phosphorus blamed for many orchard and forest fires.

title: STL closes after handing its files to a residual mechanism
why: Ended 14 years of the tribunal; convicted suspects remain at large.

title: Fires exceed 4,300 ha in the south, 500 ha elsewhere
why: Preliminary 2024 estimate separates war-zone burns from ordinary wildfires.

title: Council of State confirms Cimenterie Nationale's right to a quarry permit
why: Final ruling not applied by government; the firm reapplied in June 2025.

title: Cabinet authorises ICC Article 12(3) declaration on crimes since 7 Oct 2023
why: Would have let the ICC probe crimes on Lebanese soil; HRW praised it.

title: Lebanon backs away from the ICC declaration
why: Government chose UN complaints instead, citing confusion over the ICC's scope; no declaration was filed.

title: Salameh arrested in Lebanon after questioning
why: First detention of the ex-governor at home, on embezzlement and illicit-enrichment charges.

title: French Cour de cassation upholds jurisdiction over a Lebanese bank
why: Saradar case: French courts may hear a depositor's claim against a Lebanese bank targeting France.

title: Tyre's main water distribution facility badly damaged
why: Residents returning after the ceasefire found no running water; an example of war damage to infrastructure.

title: National Adaptation Plan 2025 lodged with UNFCCC
why: Lebanon's first NAP, covering forestry, tourism and agriculture.

title: Bitar resumes port blast probe and summons ten more officials
why: Named three port staff and seven military, security and customs officers; interrogations planned from 7 Feb.

title: New prosecutor Hajjar lets Bitar continue the case
why: Reversed the predecessor's decisions that had barred Bitar from the file.

title: World Bank rapid assessment puts reconstruction need at USD 11 billion
why: Covers 2023-24 war damage including debris and environmental cleanup.

title: Cabinet revokes special two-year quarry permit given to cement firms
why: Environment Minister Elzein told firms to apply under Decree 8803. (corrected from 2025-05 to exact date 2 May 2025; cancelled the 4 Dec 2024 decision)

title: Salameh indicted in Lebanon over central-bank funds
why: Indicted July 2025 per press; he also faces European cases including France's Optimum Invest file. (corrected from July 2025: judge charged him and referred him to trial in April 2025; further charges reported Jan 2026)

title: UNDP assesses 2024 war: 2,193 ha of forest and farmland burned
why: Data from Dec 2024 to Feb 2025: 1,917 ha forest, 275 ha farmland hit by shells and white phosphorus.

title: Lake Qaraoun shrinks as Litani inflow hits 43 million m3
why: Record low against a previous minimum of 63 million m3; drought compounds pollution.

title: Amnesty marks five years of port blast, urges unobstructed probe
why: Rights groups said political interference still blocked accountability.

title: UN Security Council votes to end UNIFIL by end-2026
why: Sets a wind-down of the peacekeeping force under Resolution 2790, with withdrawal in 2027.

title: Salameh freed on bail of about USD 14 million
why: Beirut indictment chamber set USD 20 million plus LBP 5 billion; reduced amount paid, with a travel ban.

title: 44% of Lebanon relies on water trucks in drought
why: Nearly 2 million people live in drought-prone areas; about USD 100 million needed for response.

title: Limassol court upholds jurisdiction over Lebanese banks registered in Cyprus
why: Refused to stay a USD 15 million claim despite a Lebanon-only clause.

title: National Digital Transformation and AI Strategy 2025-2030 launched
why: Policy, not statute; Lebanon still lacks a dedicated AI law beyond the MITAI draft.

title: Judge moves to question Rhosus shipowner after Bulgarian arrest
why: Key step toward the owner of the ship that brought the ammonium nitrate.

title: Drought, fires and illegal logging reported to threaten forests
why: Wire report ties the dry year to forest loss.

title: Blocs weigh a Constitutional Council challenge to the term extension
why: Bassil warned of an appeal; Council precedent says extensions must be limited and proportionate.

title: French rulings open courts to depositors of Blom Bank
why: Overturned the restrictive approach; French-domiciled depositors can sue directly in France.

title: Carnegie links Lake Qaraoun decline to migratory and farming pressures
why: Analysis of the drying reservoir and its effect on Bekaa livelihoods.

title: Salameh skips summons from Cassation judge
why: Judge Samaranda Nassar had called him on a complaint by BDL governor Souaid; a warrant followed.

title: Salameh arrested at Bhannes Hospital on a search warrant
why: New embezzlement case over commissions to Forry Associates; European authorities hold about USD 92 million in family property.

title: Lebanon accuses Israel of burning forest and farmland in south
why: Government complaint; Israeli-caused burning in 2026 put at about 7,500 ha.
